cohort: Two birth cohorts of live born infants in São Luís, Maranhão State, Brazil (2,493 infants in 1997/1998 and 5,166 infants in 2010)
finding: Despite favorable changes in socio-demographic and health service factors and decreasing rates of IUGR, perinatal mortality, and infant mortality, low birth weight and preterm birth rates remained stable, while the cesarean rate increased from 1997/1998 to 2010.
mod_finding: The study observed an increase in the cesarean section rate from 34.1% to 47.5% alongside other perinatal health trends.
